keyTerms.definition: One nested layer of the ladder. Shells 0-1 live in items 1-2, shells 2-3 in items 3-6.

recall.question: How do shells map to items, and what checks the depth gate?
recall.answer: Shells 0-1 live in items 1-2, shells 2-3 in items 3-6, shell 4 in item 7, shell 5 in item 8, shell 6 in item 9, shell 7 in item 11, shell 8 in item 10, shell 9 in item 12, shell 10 in item 13(c). Item 13 checks the depth gate.

keyTerms.definition: Every modality becomes tokens. The transformer never sees pixels, only embeddings in sequence.
Workers that generate with weight version v while trainers optimize to v+1, then broadcast.
Every artifact records its parents' hashes: a Merkle-like trail from raw data to final weights.
The gain is bounded by the stage's share. Optimizing a 3 percent stage is theater.
No single safety control is trusted. Filters catch the known-bad, sampling catches the unknown, the kill switch bounds the blast radius.
One pinned template version per training stage. Normalization is part of the template.

recall.question: What is the throughput of three pipes in series?
recall.answer: The minimum. Size each pipe to the target, then verify.

recall.question: How does the version tag keep async RL honest?
recall.answer: Rollout workers generate with weight version v, trainers optimize to v+1, then broadcast. The tag keeps the staleness honest.

recall.question: Why is a toy result a hypothesis, never a conclusion?
recall.answer: Scale changes the regime: different bottlenecks, different noise, different optima.
